steps.title: Contractual Compliance (Section 12)
steps.description: Drafting employment contracts that specify dual-currency (USD/ZiG) remuneration and adhere to Section 12 of the Labor Act, including grade classification.

steps.title: NSSA Registration
steps.description: Registering the employee with the National Social Security Authority (NSSA) and obtaining a Social Security Number for contribution tracking.

steps.title: Medical & Background Checks
steps.description: Facilitating mandatory medical examinations where required by the National Employment Council (NEC) or industry-specific safety standards.

steps.title: Training & Standards Setup
steps.description: Ensuring the employee is enrolled for ZIMDEF (Manpower Development) and SDF (Standards Development) levy reporting.

steps.title: Digital Onboarding
steps.description: Setting up the employee on digital payroll portals for tax (P6) compliance and self-service access to pay slips.

items.title: Dual-Currency Realities
items.text: Employment contracts increasingly reflect USD-denominated salaries with payments converted to ZiG at the prevailing Interbank rate to manage local inflation.

items.title: Probationary Limits
items.text: Section 12(5) limits probation to a single non-renewable 3-month period. Termination during this window requires a minimum of 2 weeks' notice.

items.title: The Role of NECs
items.text: National Employment Councils (NECs) set industry-specific minimum wages and working conditions that often override general labor law provisions.

faqs.question: Can I hire expats via EOR in Zimbabwe?
faqs.answer: Yes, but they require a Temporary Employment Permit (TEP). The EOR assists in demonstrating that no local skill matches the requirement.

faqs.question: What is the standard work week?
faqs.answer: The standard week typically ranges from 40 to 48 hours depending on the NEC sector agreement, with most offices operating 44 hours.

faqs.question: Is insurance mandatory?
faqs.answer: Statutory NSSA covers basic social security, but private medical aid (e.g., CIMAS or PSMAS) is a highly recommended benefit for top-tier talent.

items.title: 13th Month Custom
items.text: A 'Christmas bonus' or 13th-month check is a widespread cultural expectation in Zimbabwe, usually paid in November or December.

items.title: Severance Protocols
items.text: In retrenchment cases, the 2023 Amendment Act mandates a minimum package of one month's salary for every two years of service.

items.title: Union Influence
items.text: Unions are active in mining, agriculture, and industry; maintaining open communication with local shop stewards is vital for EOR compliance.

steps.title: Data Aggregation
steps.description: Collecting variable inputs (overtime, bonuses, commission) by the 20th of the month, categorized by payment currency (USD or ZiG).

steps.title: Gross-to-Net Computation
steps.description: Processing deductions for PAYE (P2), NSSA, and AIDS Levy using ZIMRA-compliant software calibrated to 4 decimal places.

steps.title: Remittance Split
steps.description: Separating tax liabilities into the ZIMRA Foreign Currency Account (for USD portions) and the Domestic Taxes Account (for ZiG portions).

steps.title: Bank File Generation
steps.description: Creating split bank files to ensure net salaries reach employees' local FCA and ZiG accounts without breaching exchange control rules.

steps.title: Statutory Filing (P2 Form)
steps.description: Submitting the monthly P2 tax return to ZIMRA by the 10th of the following month to avoid the 100% late payment penalty.

items.title: ZiG/USD Split Rules
items.text: Employers must calculate PAYE on the total value of remuneration but remit the tax in the specific currency in which the salary was paid.

items.title: The AIDS Levy Quirk
items.text: Unlike flat-rate levies, the 3% AIDS Levy is calculated on the amount of PAYE due, making accurate tax-bracket placement essential.

items.title: Interbank Exchange Rate
items.text: For statutory reporting of ZiG salaries in USD-denominated reports, the RBZ (Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe) daily Interbank rate must be utilized.

faqs.question: What happens if I miss the 10th deadline?
faqs.answer: ZIMRA enforces a 100% penalty on the principal tax amount, plus interest that compounds monthly at a rate set by the Finance Act.

faqs.question: Are bonuses taxed differently?
faqs.answer: Standard bonuses (13th month) have a tax-free threshold; amounts exceeding this are added to gross income and taxed at marginal PAYE rates.

faqs.question: Is paper filing still allowed?
faqs.answer: ZIMRA has moved toward its e-Tax portal; while paper (P2) forms are occasionally accepted in rural offices, digital filing is now the mandatory standard for most.

items.title: P6 Form Delivery
items.text: Employers are legally required to provide every employee with an annual P6 certificate summarising total earnings and tax paid by year-end.

items.title: NEC Levy Shifts
items.text: Keep a close watch on National Employment Council (NEC) circulars; levy rates often change with shorter notice than national budget items.

items.title: Holiday Pay Formulas
items.text: Calculate leave pay and holiday working rates strictly according to your specific NEC’s grading to avoid labor court disputes.

steps.title: Gross Income Input
steps.description: Capturing base salary, commissions, and taxable benefits (e.g., fuel, housing) in both USD and ZiG.

steps.title: Statutory Deductions
steps.description: Applying NSSA (4.5% up to $700 cap) and pension contributions to arrive at Taxable Income.

steps.title: PAYE Computation
steps.description: Calculating tax based on the 2025 ZIMRA tables, accounting for the tax-free threshold of $100 (approx).

steps.title: AIDS Levy Application
steps.description: Adding the mandatory 3% levy calculated specifically on the amount of PAYE due.

steps.title: Net Pay Calculation
steps.description: Deducting all taxes and levies to provide the employee's take-home pay in the respective currency.

items.title: NSSA Cap Review
items.text: The NSSA insurable earnings cap is reviewed quarterly; 2024/2025 levels are set at $700 per month.

items.title: Dual-Currency Remittance
items.text: If salary is paid in USD, taxes must be paid to ZIMRA in USD. Partial payments require proportional tax splits.

items.title: Tax-Free Bonus
items.text: The 13th-month bonus typically enjoys a specific tax-free threshold (reviewed annually in the National Budget).

faqs.question: Can I calculate ZiG tax?
faqs.answer: Yes, the calculator uses the latest ZIMRA tables for both USD and ZiG currencies as per current Statutory Instruments.

faqs.question: Are benefits-in-kind taxable?
faqs.answer: Yes, fuel, housing, and school fees benefits are taxable under the 'Deemed Benefit' rules of the Income Tax Act.

faqs.question: What is the AIDS Levy?
faqs.answer: It is a 3% levy calculated on the PAYE amount, effectively a tax on a tax, used for HIV/AIDS prevention programs.

items.title: NEC Graded Minimums
items.text: Ensure your base salary meets the minimums set by the relevant National Employment Council (NEC) for your sector.

items.title: P6 Form Delivery
items.text: Employers must provide an annual P6 certificate to every employee by the end of the first month of the new tax year.

items.title: Pension Deductions
items.text: In addition to NSSA, many firms have mandatory private pension contributions which should be factored into the 'Net Pay' logic.

steps.title: Statutory Drafting
steps.description: Preparing the Memorandum and Articles of Association (for PLCs) or the Incorporation Statement (for PBCs).

steps.title: Capital & Bank Setup
steps.description: Setting up the mandatory Foreign Currency Account (FCA) and domestic account for capital injection and operational use.

steps.title: Tax & Social Security Linkage
steps.description: Registering for the Business Partner (BP) number with ZIMRA and the NSSA employer code for statutory compliance.

items.title: ZIDA Facilitation
items.text: Foreign investors should leverage the Zimbabwe Investment and Development Agency (ZIDA) to streamline work permits and licensing in a single window.

items.title: Local Director custom
items.text: While not always legally mandated for all sectors, having a local resident director significantly eases bank account opening and ZIMRA physical inspections.

items.title: Beneficial Ownership
items.text: Recent 2024 regulations require strict disclosure of beneficial owners (holding >20% shares) to the Registrar of Companies.

faqs.question: How long does name reservation take?
faqs.answer: Name reservation typically takes 2-4 business days, though expedited services at the Registrar of Companies can reduce this.

faqs.question: Can I operate as a sole trader?
faqs.answer: Foreigners are generally restricted from operating as sole traders and must incorporate a PBC or PLC to comply with investment regulations.

faqs.question: What is the minimum capital?
faqs.answer: There is no statutory minimum capital for PLCs, but practical banking requirements usually suggest an injection of at least $500 - $1,000.

items.title: Reserved Sectors 2025
items.text: Certain sectors like retail and passenger transport are reserved for Zimbabwean citizens unless specific investment thresholds are met via ZIDA.

items.title: PBC for SMEs
items.text: Private Business Corporations (PBCs) are often faster to set up and have lower compliance overhead for small-to-medium enterprises.

items.title: ZIDA One-Stop Shop
items.text: The ZIDA office in Harare provides a single point for company registration, tax, and licensing, significantly speeding up the entry process.

steps.title: Academic Verification
steps.description: Validating degrees from the University of Zimbabwe (UZ) and NUST through the Zimbabwe Council for Higher Education (ZIMCHE).

steps.title: Bilingual Assessment

steps.title: Onboarding Coordination

items.title: The Diaspora Return
items.text: Many high-tier roles are currently being filled by returning 'diaspora' Zimbabweans with regional (SA/UK) experience.

items.title: LinkedIn Engagement
items.text: Harare's professional community is exceptionally active on LinkedIn; direct headhunting is often more effective than job board postings.

items.title: Hard Skills Scarcity
items.text: Specialized roles in FinTech (blockchain, React) and heavy industry often face scarcity, requiring aggressive talent mapping.

faqs.question: What is the typical notice period?
faqs.answer: Notice periods vary by seniority and contract type, usually ranging from 1 to 3 months for permanent positions.

faqs.question: Are background checks common?
faqs.answer: Yes, criminal record checks via the Republic Police and verification of academic transcripts from ZIMSEC or local universities are standard.

faqs.question: Is the 13th-month bonus mandatory?
faqs.answer: While not statutory, a 'December Bonus' is a deeply entrenched market expectation and is often included in NEC agreements.

items.title: Detailed CVs
items.text: Zimbabwean candidates typically provide very detailed CVs including full academic history (O-Levels/A-Levels) and personal references.

items.title: Educational Verification
items.text: Given the high value placed on education, strictly verifying degrees and certificates is essential to avoid fraudulent credentials.

items.title: Mobile First Reach
items.text: Professional recruitment often happens on LinkedIn, but lower-level roles are effectively sourced through WhatsApp groups and community notices.

steps.title: System Selection
steps.description: Evaluating systems like Belina or Sage that support Zimbabwe's complex ZIMRA tax tables and dual-currency (USD/ZiG) reporting.

steps.title: Grade Mapping
steps.description: Configuring NEC (National Employment Council) job grades and corresponding salary structures into the HRIS database.

steps.title: Employee Self-Service
steps.description: Setting up mobile portals for payslip viewing, P6 certificate downloads, and leave requests (statutory and annual).

steps.title: NSSA & Tax Integration

steps.title: Policy Digitalization

items.title: Offline Connectivity
items.text: Given intermittent power/internet in some regions, 'Offline-first' desktop systems with cloud sync are still preferred by many local HR managers.

items.title: Dual-Bank Output
items.text: Systems must generate separate bank export files for FCA (USD) and local (ZiG) accounts to comply with exchange control regulations.

items.title: ZIMRA e-Tax Ready
items.text: Ensure your HRIS can export the P2 file in the exact Excel structure required by the ZIMRA portal to avoid manual data entry errors.

faqs.question: Can the HRIS handle dual currency?
faqs.answer: Yes, local-ready HRIS systems are designed to calculate payroll and taxes in both USD and ZiG simultaneously.

faqs.question: Is cloud hosting safe?
faqs.answer: Cloud hosting is growing, but ensure compliance with the 2021 Data Protection Act regarding the transfer of personal data outside Zimbabwe.

faqs.question: Does it support biometric integration?
faqs.answer: Many industrial firms in Zimbabwe use biometric clock-in systems integrated directly with their HRIS for attendance tracking.

items.title: Connectivity Resilience
items.text: Systems should have mobile app capability and offline-sync features to handle sporadic internet connectivity or power load-shedding.

items.title: Data Sovereignty
items.text: Recent data laws emphasize that critical citizen data should ideally reside within local jurisdiction or be handled by certified providers.

items.title: Self-Service Adoption
items.text: Employee self-service (ESS) via WhatsApp-based bots is highly effective in Zimbabwe due to the platform's ubiquitous usage and low data cost.

steps.title: Daily Exchange Sync
steps.description: Recording daily RBZ Interbank rates to ensure accurate multi-currency valuation for reporting.

steps.title: VAT Reporting

steps.title: Statutory Audit Prep

steps.title: Tax Computation (QPDs)

items.title: IFRS for SMEs
items.text: Most medium-sized entities in Zimbabwe utilize 'IFRS for SMEs' to simplify disclosure requirements while maintaining global credibility.

items.title: Hyperinflation Accounting
items.text: Accountants must remain vigilant regarding IAS 29 (Financial Reporting in Hyperinflationary Economies) if local currency volatility thresholds are exceeded.

items.title: IMTT Reconciliation
items.text: The 2% money transfer tax is a significant overhead; meticulous reconciliation is needed to separate tax-exempt transfers from taxable ones.

faqs.question: What is the financial year end?
faqs.answer: The standard tax year end is December 31st, though companies can apply to ZIMRA for a different financial year-end.

faqs.question: Is software mandatory?
faqs.answer: While not legally mandatory, ZIMRA audits strongly favor digital records from systems like Xero, QuickBooks, or Sage.

faqs.question: Can I report only in USD?
faqs.answer: Statutory accounts must often show a conversion to the local currency (ZiG) for ZIMRA, even if the functional business currency is USD.

items.title: RBZ Exchange Rate
items.text: Always use the official Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe (RBZ) interbank rate for currency conversions to avoid discrepancies with ZIMRA.

items.title: IFRS 16 Leases
items.text: For entities with significant leased assets (e.g., vehicles, property), ensure compliance with IFRS 16 for proper balance sheet recognition.

items.title: Digital Record Keeping
items.text: ZIMRA increasingly prefers digital records and e-filing; invest in accounting software that facilitates this for smoother audits.

steps.title: KYC/AML Alignment
steps.description: Registering with the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) for sectors prone to high-value transactions.

steps.title: Exchange Control Compliance
steps.description: Engaging an Authorised Dealer (Bank) to register external loans or management fees with the RBZ.

steps.title: NSSA Safety Audit
steps.description: Facilitating annual workplace safety inspections to maintain compliance with the Factories and Works Act.

steps.title: Beneficial Ownership Filing
steps.description: Submitting the mandatory disclosure of ultimate owners to the Registrar of Companies.

steps.title: Data Privacy Setup
steps.description: Aligning internal data handling with the Cyber Security and Data Protection Act (Chapter 12:07).

items.title: RBZ Exchange Control
items.text: All outward remittances (dividends, consulting fees) require prior approval or registration with the Reserve Bank's Exchange Control Division.

items.title: Data Protection
items.text: Zimbabwe's 2021 Data Protection Act imposes strict requirements on the cross-border transfer of sensitive employee personal data.

items.title: Statutory Instrument (SI) Velocity
items.text: Regulations in Zimbabwe often change via 'Statutory Instruments' overnight; maintaining a local compliance partner is critical.

items.title: NSSA Compliance
items.text: Mandatory registration and monthly contributions for all employees; failure leads to stiff penalties and interest.

items.title: AML/KYC Requirements
items.text: Under the Money Laundering and Proceeds of Crime Act, businesses must maintain robust records of beneficial ownership.

items.title: Exchange Control
items.text: Compliance with RBZ directives (e.g., SI 127) regarding currency usage and pricing is strictly monitored.

items.title: ZimCode
items.text: The National Code on Corporate Governance Zimbabwe (ZimCode) provides the framework for best practices.

items.title: Penalties for Delay
items.text: Late filing of ZIMRA or NSSA returns attracts heavy punitive interest, often calculated daily.

items.title: Data Protection Officer
items.text: Large entities handling personal data are increasingly expected to appoint a designated Data Protection Officer (DPO).

faqs.question: Are there local content requirements?
faqs.answer: In sectors like mining and government procurement, 'Indigenisation' or local content policies may apply; consult ZIDA for your specific industry.

faqs.question: What is the penalty for non-compliance?
faqs.answer: Penalties for exchange control or tax breaches can include heavy fines, asset forfeiture, or criminal prosecution for directors.

faqs.question: Is an IPEC registration needed?
faqs.answer: Only if your entity provides insurance or pension services; otherwise, typical corporates interact primarily with ZIMRA and NSSA.

steps.title: Registration
steps.description: Obtaining a Business Partner (BP) Number and registering for various tax heads (Income Tax, VAT, PAYE).

steps.title: QPD Submission
steps.description: Paying Quarterly Payment Dates (QPDs) on the 25th of March, June, September, and December (10%, 25%, 30%, 35% ratio).

steps.title: VAT Filing
steps.description: Electronic submission of VAT 7 returns by the 25th of the month following the transaction period.

steps.title: Final Return (ITF 12C)
steps.description: Submitting the final Corporate Income Tax return by April 30th (or later if extension granted) for the prior tax year.

steps.title: Tax Clearance (ITF 263)
steps.description: Obtaining the annual ITF 263 certificate, essential for avoiding the 30% withholding tax on payments from clients.

items.title: 30% Withholding Hazard
items.text: Without a valid ITF 263 (Tax Clearance Code), clients are legally required to withhold 30% of your gross invoice amount.

items.title: Mutapa Investment Fund
items.text: Entities involved with or competing against Mutapa Fund subsidiaries should note specific tax exemptions that may impact market dynamics.

items.title: Currency of Payment
items.text: Taxes must generally be remitted in the currency of the transaction; USD income generates a USD tax liability.

faqs.question: Is there a wealth tax?
faqs.answer: Zimbabwe introduced a 'Wealth Tax' on residential properties above a certain value in 2024; businesses should assess property-holding impacts.

faqs.question: What is the penalty for late VAT?
faqs.answer: Late VAT filing triggers a penalty of up to 100% of the tax due, similar to PAYE penalties.

faqs.question: Are exports tax-exempt?
faqs.answer: Exports are generally zero-rated for VAT, and companies in Special Economic Zones (SEZs) may enjoy corporate tax holidays.

items.title: Double Tax Agreements (DTAs)
items.text: Zimbabwe has DTAs with many countries, including South Africa, UK, and UAE; utilizing these can reduce withholding tax on dividends.

items.title: Audit Frequency
items.text: ZIMRA conducts periodic 'desk audits' and full field audits; maintaining clean digital trails of all local transactions is vital.

items.title: Fiscalization Requirements
items.text: Registered operators must use fiscal devices (point of sale) to record all transactions, ensuring real-time reporting to ZIMRA.

steps.title: Jurisdiction Selection

steps.title: Currency Specification

steps.title: Data Protection Clause

steps.title: Termination Protocal

steps.title: Indemnification & HIPAA
steps.description: Drafting robust indemnity clauses to protect against regulatory shifts and exchange control breaches.

items.title: Contractor vs Employee
items.text: Zimbabwean courts often use the 'control test'; if a contractor works exclusively for you using your tools, they may be deemed a 'statutory employee' with full benefits.

items.title: Arbitration Preference
items.text: Many international firms prefer the Commercial Arbitration Centre in Harare for faster resolution compared to the High Court backlog.

items.title: Dual-Language Contracts
items.text: While English is the legal standard, having simplified summaries in Shona/Ndebele for manual labor contracts is a best practice for clarity.

faqs.question: What is the statute of limitations?
faqs.answer: The standard prescription period for most contractual debts in Zimbabwe is 3 years from the date the debt became due.

faqs.question: Are e-signatures valid?
faqs.answer: Yes, under the Electronic Transactions and Cybersecurity Act, digital signatures are generally recognized for commercial contracts.

faqs.question: Do I need a local legal representative?
faqs.answer: Foreign entities are strongly advised to have a local Legal Practitioner (admitted to the High Court) for process service and regulatory liaison.

items.title: Witness Requirements
items.text: Commercial contracts usually require two witnesses per party for enhanced evidentiary value in local courts.

items.title: Stamp Duty
items.text: Certain types of legal documents and property-related contracts may attract stamp duty at the Deeds Office.

items.title: Company Resolution
items.text: Ensure that the signatory has a valid Board Resolution authorizing them to bind the Zimbabwean entity.

items.title: Mediation Clauses
items.text: Including a tier-1 mediation clause can save significant costs by avoiding immediate litigation in the High Court.

items.title: Currency of Award
items.text: Arbitration awards can be denominated in USD, but enforcement may be subject to the prevailing exchange control regulations.

items.title: Language for Translation
items.text: For contracts involving significant rural workforces, bilingual summaries in Shona/Ndebele are recommended for clarity.

items.title: FinTech Focus

faqs.question: Are software licenses taxed?

items.title: Mobile Money APIs

items.title: Connectivity Tiers

items.title: WhatsApp Marketing

items.title: Influencer Impact

faqs.question: Are there advertising restrictions?
faqs.answer: Yes, products like alcohol and pharmaceuticals have strict ZIMRAT or MCAZ-regulated advertising guidelines.

faqs.question: What is the best time to run ads?
faqs.answer: Peak engagement times are usually early morning and late evening, aligned with commuter traffic and leisure time.

faqs.question: Do I need color-coded messaging?
faqs.answer: Given political sensitivities, certain colors (like red, yellow, or green) should be used thoughtfully in broad-reach corporate branding.

items.title: Bilingualism
items.text: Content that mixes English with Shona and Ndebele slang ('Chi-Street') resonates deeply with the urban youth demographic.

items.title: Data Bundles
items.text: Zimbabweans are very conscious of data costs; images and videos should be optimized for low-bandwidth to encourage sharing.

items.title: Radio Reach
items.text: Never underestimate the power of morning drive-time radio for reaching decision-makers in high-traffic CBD areas.
